  "topic": "Blood Relations and Family Trees",

  "answer": "C",

    "A) Brother‑in‑law",
    "B) Cousin-in-law",
    "C) No standard direct relation (affinal chain only)",
    "D) Nephew-in-law"
  ]
}

  "topic": "Blood Relations and Family Trees",

  "explanation": "Whether S is the child of R’s maternal uncle or paternal uncle, S is the child of a parent’s brother. That relation to R is always a first cousin.",
  "answer": "B",
  "choices": [
    "A) Nephew/Niece",
    "B) First cousin",
    "C) First cousin once removed",
    "D) Not uniquely determinable"
  ]
}

  "topic": "Blood Relations and Family Trees",
  "question": "“Pointing to a man, I say: \"He is the only son of my mother, I am the only daughter of my mother, and I have no brothers\"; under the standard meaning of \"only\" and monogamy, who is he to me?”",
  "explanation": "“If I have no brothers, then my mother has no sons. That directly contradicts \"He is the only son of my mother.\" The constraints cannot all hold; the scenario is impossible.”",
  "answer": "C",
